I've been farming these 9.5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Me and my wife, we're the only ones working it now. I split the land into 6.5 mu for wheat-maize and 3 mu for cotton. That's what I've always done, and I don't see a reason to change.

For the wheat, I plant in mid-October after rotary tilling the land. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's 50 kg a bag. Then when the wheat turns green in March, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once at green-up, and once at jointing. Two sprays — one for weeds right after planting, one for insects in spring. Last year I got about 470 kg per mu. This year if the weather is normal I expect about 480 kg per mu.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed right after the wheat comes off in mid-June. There's no time to plough — the season is too tight — so I use no-tillage planting. At planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and at the big trumpet stage I spread about 15 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain doesn't come. Two sprays for pests. I expect about 520 kg per mu.

For cotton, I plough in spring and plant hybrid cotton in late April. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress twice with urea, about 7 or 8 kg each time. Cotton needs more care — I irrigate three times and spray four times because bollworm and aphids are always a problem. I hope for about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer got expensive again this year, but I don't dare cut back. Old Wang down the road uses about the same amounts, and his yields are steady. Better to waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — a bad year means real trouble for us. Me and my wife do all the work ourselves, except sometimes we hire a few people for wheat harvest and cotton picking when it's busy.
